latest_final: The puzzle turns on the double meaning of "course." The narrator is a genuinely smart and attentive classroom student enrolled in an academic course, but they could not "pass the course" because "course" also denotes a physical watercourse—a waterway or channel—and "pass" there means to get past or across it. The acknowledged failure involved not being able to get past that named water course, so the student never completed the academic class. The waterway is not merely a wording trick: it is a real obstacle connected to the failure. It was not a flood, a difficult commute, a swim test, a boating or sports class, a river-crossing field exercise, drowning, or an administrative error. In short, the student failed the academic class because the same "course" was a physical waterway they could not pass, so they could not successfully pass the course in the school sense either.
